parameters.subject: =Agent wants approval: {{ $json.action }}

nodes.name: Ask Human (Slack)
nodes.notes: Slack sendAndWait renders parameters.message — a `text` key on this operation is stored and silently IGNORED (found live 2026-08-17). Approval mode offers exactly two buttons, which is why the third outcome (Adjust) is reached through the Reject branch rather than a third button: that makes 'adjust' structurally a NON-approval rather than a sibling of approval.

nodes.name: Decision (fail closed)
nodes.notes: Unchanged by the adjust-path work of 2026-08-21 and must stay that way: test-ask-human-gate.mjs reads this jsCode out of this file and holds it to 19 cases with exactly one path to approved:true. The Adjust outcome is derived downstream, on this node's FALSE branch only.

nodes.name: Approved?
nodes.notes: Strict boolean equality against the fail-closed decision. The FALSE branch is the only way to reach the adjust path, so no adjustment can ever be routed into the approve branch.

parameters.subject: =Rejected — adjust or deny: {{ $('Shape Proposal').first().json.action }}
parameters.message:
=You rejected that proposal, so the agent is *not* proceeding. One more line decides what happens next.

*Type an adjustment* — e.g. "only 10 leads, OryonIQ only" — and the agent revises its plan and comes back here for a fresh approval. An adjustment is NOT an approval: nothing runs until you press Approve on the revised plan.
*Type DENY, or don't reply* — the agent stops and logs why.

Typing "approved" here does nothing. The Approve button is the only approval channel.

nodes.name: Ask Reason (Slack)
nodes.notes: Reached only after a NON-approval, so nothing downstream of here can approve. limitWaitTime is set so a rejection that never gets its follow-up line times out into DENY instead of hanging the execution forever — unlike the first ask, where waiting indefinitely IS the safe state. Uses .first() rather than .item on Shape Proposal: paired-item linkage does not survive the IF node (same trap as WF-1's Classify node), and this branch always carries exactly one proposal.

nodes.name: Tool Response (fail closed)
nodes.notes: Last node executed, so this is what the calling agent receives back from the sub-workflow tool. Both branches feed input index 0; exactly one ever carries data.
